cases.reason: Before: `if unobserved:` routes only runs with unobserved tests to NOT_ATTEMPTED, so a completed run with no red tests falls through to SURVIVED. After: `if not unobserved:` sends a fully completed, no-red run to NOT_ATTEMPTED, so the non-discrimination conclusion is never recorded for it, which is the defective behavior.

Before: line 643 passes `mutation_attempts=attempts` into Review, so survived attempts reach the stored review (expected). After: line 643 is unchanged and still wires attempts; the edit only changes line 641 from `pair_verdicts=verdicts` to `pair_mapping.verdicts`, a different field, so mutation attempts are still propagated and the defective behaviour is not introduced.

BEFORE: line 274 `if execution is None or not execution.enabled: return [], [], []` skips establish_baseline unless execution.enabled is true, which is the defective behaviour. AFTER: line 274 only returns early when `execution is None`, so the baseline now runs whenever settings exist even if disabled. It is still skipped when execution is None, and it runs the mutations too, so it is neither the expected behaviour for every review nor the defective one.

Before: line 145 uses `outcome.reason or "..."`, so the execution-stage reason is preserved and the canned text is only a fallback when none exists. After: line 145 always uses the canned string, discarding `outcome.reason`, so the record can misstate why the test did not settle.

Before: the validator at line 127 raises ValueError when `not self.settled and not has_reason`, so unsettled attempts with an empty reason are rejected. After: line 127 becomes `if False and ...`, so the check never fires and a non-settling MutationAttempt with an empty reason is accepted, which is the defective behaviour.

Before: the NOT_ATTEMPTED MutationAttempt at lines 179-185 stores reason=_why_unobserved(unobserved, result.outcomes), so the runner's reason is preserved. After: line 184 sets reason="", which drops the produced reason and leaves it empty, matching the defective behaviour.

BEFORE: line 136 calls _set_aside_block(review), whose body is not shown, so whether it names each test and its reason cannot be confirmed. AFTER: lines 135-137 append only the generic note 'Candidate tests were set aside.' with no test names or reasons, which is the DEFECTIVE behaviour.

Before: line 509 passes only `pair_mapping.unjudged` to `derive_support`, and the code shown never says whether set-aside failing tests are already absent from `verdicts` (line 479), so it cannot be decided. After: line 509 adds `set_aside_tests` entries to the unjudged input, but `set_aside_tests` is not defined here, the `discovered.tests` filter is unclear, and it is unknown how `derive_support` treats unjudged entries, so the effect on set-aside tests cannot be confirmed.

Before, line 457 calls _run_execution_tier(...) ahead of judge_pairs, so execution runs first when enabled. After, that call is replaced by `attempts, executed_verdicts, set_aside_tests = [], [], []`, so the execution-stage function is never invoked and judge_pairs (the static judgement) runs on all defect sets as the effective first stage.

BEFORE: line 952 `enabled=args.execute` gates execution on the opt-in flag, so without --execute the static judgement stays first, which is the DEFECTIVE behaviour. AFTER: line 952 hardcodes `enabled=False`, so execution never precedes the code-reading judgement even with --execute; this disables execution entirely rather than making it the default, so it is neither EXPECTED nor the DEFECTIVE 'only when --execute is set' behaviour.

Before, judge_pairs receives remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets), so defects execution could not settle still reach the static judgement and the verdicts are merged at `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts`. After, line 465 passes `[]`, so the static judge is given no defects and unsettled defects get no code-reading judgement, which is the DEFECTIVE behaviour of returning without static judgement for them.

BEFORE, line 284-285 raises ReviewHalted when baseline.halted, so the review stops and unsettled defects never reach the static judgement. AFTER, line 285 returns [], [], baseline.set_aside instead, so the pipeline continues and the defects remain unsettled and go on to the static judgement (remaining_defect_sets is the identity with no verdicts).

Before, line 85 removes only defects with attempt.settled from the sets passed to static judgement, so unsettled defects remain in a form the judgement can consume. After, line 85 drops the `if attempt.settled` filter, so every attempted defect, including unsettled ones, is removed from the static judgement input and the code-reading conclusion is never recorded for them. That matches the defective behaviour of unsettled defects never being converted into the static judgement input.

Before, the validator `_a_settled_attempt_injected_something` raises when `self.settled and self.descriptor is None`, so every settled attempt must carry a descriptor. After, the check is `self.outcome is MutationOutcomeKind.KILLED and self.descriptor is None`, so settled outcomes other than KILLED (e.g. survived) can exist with no descriptor, which is the defective behaviour.

Before: lines 105-111 return _not_mutable when `regions` is empty, before any sources, descriptor or execution. Lines 113-116 then return _not_mutable before `build_descriptor` or `run_tests`, so the defect is still rejected mechanically before execution, only with a different message.

BEFORE: line 479 merges `executed_verdicts` (from `_run_execution_tier`) into `verdicts` that feed `derive_support`, but the code shown does not reveal whether those verdicts encode executed lines or only test outcomes/mutation results, so the behaviour cannot be decided. BEFORE: `if parse is not None:` wraps the parse check, so a file with no parser skips it and falls through to `return None` (valid). AFTER: `if parse is None: return ... is not mutable: no parser available` makes parser absence a rejection, which is exactly the defective behaviour.

AFTER, the `.json: json.loads` entry is removed, leaving only .py and .pyi, so a broken .json is no longer parsed and can pass validity, which is the DEFECTIVE behaviour.

Before: the `except _PARSE_ERRORS as error:` branch at line 132-133 returns a rejection message when parsing fails, so the edit is marked invalid. After: the except block is just `pass`, so a parse error falls through to `return None` at line 135, meaning the edit is accepted as valid.

BEFORE: lines 461-474 call judge_pairs(remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets), ...) after the execution tier, so the code-reading judgement stays wired in and runs for the defects execution did not settle. BEFORE: judge_pairs gets only remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets), so settled defects skip the code-reading judgement, and line 479 `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts` puts execution verdicts in their place. After, line 285 `return [], [], baseline.set_aside` no longer raises, so the pipeline continues with no attempts or verdicts, the same as the execution-off path, and the existing review logic runs.

Before: line 465 sends only the defects injection could not reach to the static judge, and line 479 `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts` keeps those static conclusions alongside the executed ones. After: line 479 `verdicts = executed_verdicts` drops pair_mapping.verdicts, so the static verdicts for unsettled defects are discarded and only execution-stage outcomes feed derive_support, which alters the static conclusions instead of preserving them.

Before: line 479 builds `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts`, and that combined list reaches `derive_support` on line 509. After: line 479 is `verdicts = pair_mapping.verdicts`, so `derive_support` gets only the static pair verdicts and executed DEFECT_KILLED evidence cannot affect the recorded tier.

BEFORE: `_achieved_tier` returns `min(...)` over each defect's tier, with unanswered defects defaulting to STATIC, so one STATIC verdict pulls the whole criterion down to STATIC. AFTER: line 277 uses `max(...)`, so any DEFECT_KILLED verdict raises the recorded tier. This assumes `EvidenceTier` orders STATIC below DEFECT_KILLED, which the enum definition (not shown) would confirm. The docstring still says 'weakest', but that is stale text and does not change behaviour.

Before, _set_aside_block emits `[{test.kind.value}] {test.test_id}` for each set-aside test, so the tests are named. After, line 314 drops `test.test_id`, leaving only the kind and reason, so the section shows tests were set aside without their ids or names.

AFTER, line 36 `start_line <= self.start_line and self.end_line <= end_line` reverses it, so it accepts edits that enclose the region (including spans outside it) and rejects spans strictly inside it.

Before, line 104 rejects any edit with line_count > max_edit_lines, enforcing a bound that pushes toward the smallest edit. After, line 104 uses max_edit_lines * 2, so edits up to twice the bound are accepted, which means a larger non-minimal edit that still makes the defect true is now accepted.

AFTER: line 952 hardcodes enabled=False, so execution is always disabled, the static path is always used, and no edit is ever built or applied, which is the DEFECTIVE behaviour.

Before: line 170 builds `offered` from only the pre-resolved regions, line 171 constrains region_label to those labels plus "", and the subject shows only those regions, so candidate edits are limited to predeclared regions (defective). That disables the whole stage rather than expanding candidates beyond the regions, so it is neither the expected behaviour nor the defective restriction-to-regions one.

Before, line 39 sets `allow_failing_tests: bool = False`, so by default a red candidate test halts the review as the docstring describes. After, line 39 sets it to `True`, so failing candidate tests are set aside by default and the review proceeds without halting, which is the defective behaviour.

Before: line 284-285 `if baseline.halted: raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` stops the pipeline on a halted baseline. After: line 285 is `pass`, so a halted baseline falls through to build descriptors and run_mutations and returns verdicts without reporting the halt.

AFTER, that check and raise are removed, so the failure stays only in `Baseline.halted`/`halt_reason` and the pipeline continues into run_mutations without stopping, which is the defective behaviour.

After: line 284 becomes `if baseline.halted and execution.allow_failing_tests:`, so when failing tests are not allowed (the case that should halt) no raise happens and execution continues into run_mutations at line 292, which is the defective behaviour.

After: lines 62-63 hardcode kills=False, so a failing test is no longer linked as a killer even though tier stays DEFECT_KILLED; this is the wrong tier/kills shape, and the verdict does not read as discriminating.

BEFORE, line 64 in verdicts_from() builds PairVerdict with tier=EvidenceTier.DEFECT_KILLED for settled attempts, which is the defective behaviour. AFTER, line 64 sets tier=EvidenceTier.STATIC, so the records from this path are stored at the weaker tier as expected.

BEFORE passes `execution=execution` into `run_review` (line 209), so the configured execution settings, presumably including continue-anyway, reach the pipeline; the construction of `execution` is not shown, so this is inferred. That probably disables the execution tier and baseline run altogether, not the narrower defect of a baseline that runs with continuing disabled, so I answer other.

Before: `settled` is built only from `attempt.settled`, and the new `or` clause would be redundant if that already covered NOT_ATTEMPTED, so those defects stay in the set given to static judgement (the `settled` definition isn't shown, so this is inferred). In both versions the halt on baseline failure happens before descriptors are built or any mutation validity check runs, and `build_descriptors`/`run_mutations` are unchanged. The edit at line 284 only adds `and not execution.allow_failing_tests` to the existing halt condition, which restates what `establish_baseline` already receives. It does not make validity depend on test-run control flow, so mechanical checks still decide descriptor validity and execution settings only gate whether execution runs.

Before: _parser_for loops over _PARSERS and matches by endswith, so only the hardcoded suffixes in the table get a parser; other parseable types return None and skip the parse check. After: line 139 does an exact-key lookup in the same _PARSERS table using the extension, so it is still limited to the hardcoded extensions and no parser is added for unlisted types. The edit only changes the matching method, so the defective behaviour remains.

Before, _reason returns past-tense observed statements ('The test failed when the defect was injected.', 'still passed when the defect was injected'). It still stores one path, one start, one end and one replacement, so the edit does not nest spans or drop the boundaries, and it is not the DEFECTIVE shape; it is a different bug (wrong end line).

BEFORE, the ReviewHalted handler at line 964 prints `{exc}` (the halt reason) to stderr, so the reason reaches the caller.
